The default CSS for vote looks, in my opinion, constricted in larger resolutions. This is mostly because #container and #header-banner are set to

max-width: 1200px; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;.

At screen resolutions at 1920x1080 and higher it makes the page smaller than it could be. I played around with it a bit, removing these rules, and re-sizing my screen. I didn't notice anything wrong when removing these rules. Is there any reason to keep them? Am I the only one who thinks it would look better if the site displayed at full width?

The purpose of the container layout is to displace the whitespace that existed in the middle of the posts and comments and the sidebar to the outsides so everything was in the middle and didn't require much cursor movement to go from one side to the other. Prior to a few changes with image expandos, there was a max-width value for comments to prevent lines from getting too long and making it hard to read. With that max width that was in place, there was little difference in terms of whitespace between the container layout and the full-width.

The reason it is not an option to go back to the full-width layout is because of that missing max-width value (and also because the whitespace would separate everything again). Basically, there is no logical reason to go full-width anymore. Which is why if users want that inferior layout, they will need to add it via a third-party plugin, addon, or extension.

Similar threads: (140434) (125365) (123905) (121974)

Okay, I completely understand. That's a smart thing to do, but wouldn't a percentage be a better choice for that property? 1200px, being a fixed value, looks really constricted on larger monitors. A value such as 70% - 85% provides a more flexible layout across larger displays.

It's because of the missing max-width property to comments. Without it, lines would become too long, which affects readability (even Reddit puts that property on that comment). Like I said before: the container width will not be expanded unless the max-width is in place. But, since that would be in place, you'd again be putting the whitespace back inside which would completely defeat the purpose of the container.

To put it simply, the container cannot be removed. Especially for a reason like "it looks constricted" (a useless opinion). If users want a less 'constrained' look, they will have to zoom in.
